block_fields.name: beta
block_fields.note: bundling strength in [0, 1]; the GLSL's u_beta push constant

block_fields.name: stride
block_fields.note: control points allocated per edge; the GLSL's u_stride, carried as a float because block_buffer uploads float32

bindings.name: ctrl
bindings.note: array<vec4<f32>>: `stride` control points per edge, edge after edge. xyz is the point; the .w of an edge's first point is that edge's control point count, which is variable. The GLSL reads the same array from a 2D texture tiled into rows of 4096 (u_ctrl_row), which exists only because Blender's gpu module has no SSBO; the index arithmetic is otherwise unchanged. The caller must build the buffer with STORAGE usage -- Renderer.block_buffer only makes UNIFORM buffers today.

doc: Hierarchical edge bundling with the cubic B-spline evaluated by de Boor's algorithm in the vertex shader, one instance per edge over a control polygon of variable length. There is no sample vertex buffer, so the sample count is `expand.vertex_count` here and the SAMPLES constant in heb_line.wgsl, and the two must agree. `expand.mode` says "instanced_quad" because that is the only mode the loader accepts; nothing here is a quad, and "instanced_primitive" would be the accurate name for what README 1.1 says the mode does.
spec_builder: none yet -- the engine has no heb_line MeshSpec builder; SciGraphs/ui/gpu_render/heb_gpu.py::build is the Blender-side equivalent and tests/test_heb_line.py builds the spec by hand
